rules_check.verdict: Most of the quiet scheme can ship as a design change. No ADR touches it. No D-0xx founder decision requires the dagger, warning ink or the strip under the KPI cards: the Calculation Provenance Rule and the † came from #1191's design work, not a founder decision. The founder's 2026-10-10 analysis decisions (letters as the note mark, the period vocabulary, the glyph budget, "Unavailable" / "No figures need review") all stay compatible. No marketing, pricing, legal or brand promise depends on a visible per-figure mark. The PR must still update a lot together: DESIGN.md's rule with the .impeccable/design.json sidecar (designSnapshotParity), the Data note mark, Analysis table, Data notes strip and §10 entries in frontend/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md, the reconciliation lesson, the superseded parts of the redesign doc, this branch's own coherence.md and prototype, the in-product copy that names the † (NarrativePane:121, DataNotes:103), the landing demo and teaser layout, and the unit, e2e and backend export tests that pin daggers, legacy and unavailable letters and the strip's place. One item needs the founder's explicit word first. Item 2 removes the on-figure letter from figures whose stored validation is needs_review (legacy_calculation), from unavailable values and from figures with no validation record. The redesign records this as the founder's "never hide a note", and a P0 review enforced it for exactly this case. The founder's message leans this way, so a one-line confirmation recorded as a decision (narrowing the rule to "every note stays in the dialog and the data notes; only notes that question the number keep a mark") is enough. Keep this presentation-only: the note kind and totals stay as they are, legacy figures are never shown as validated, and the fine print never says "No figures need review" while a legacy note exists. Reclassifying legacy_calculation in the backend would change what counts as needs_review, a separate founder call that also breaks the strict note-kind decoder for tabs already open. The rest is design scope: decide whether the Q4 column-header and period-picker daggers stay, and handle the letters stored in saved snapshots, where a legacy note can keep "a" while the only visible letter is "b".
